### onSend
If you are using the `onSend` hook, you can change the payload. For example:

```js
fastify.addHook('onSend', (request, reply, payload, done) => {
  const err = null;
  const newPayload = payload.replace('some-text', 'some-new-text')
  done(err, newPayload)
})
```
Or `async/await`:
```js
fastify.addHook('onSend', async (request, reply, payload) => {
  const newPayload = payload.replace('some-text', 'some-new-text')
  return newPayload
})
```

You can also clear the payload to send a response with an empty body by
replacing the payload with `null`:

```js
fastify.addHook('onSend', (request, reply, payload, done) => {
  reply.code(304)
  const newPayload = null
  done(null, newPayload)
})
```

> You can also send an empty body by replacing the payload with the empty string
> `''`, but be aware that this will cause the `Content-Length` header to be set
> to `0`, whereas the `Content-Length` header will not be set if the payload is
> `null`.

> ℹ️ Note:
> If you change the payload, you may only change it to a `string`, a
> `Buffer`, a `stream`, a `ReadableStream`, a `Response`, or `null`.

Report a conflict only when two sections make incompatible statements about the SAME option, flag, default value, limit, version requirement, or behavior, for the same product version and scope. These are NOT conflicts: values of different options; example values in code samples that merely override a default; statements explicitly scoped to an older version or to migration history; one section giving more detail than the other; different defaults that the text ties to different contexts (per-route vs global, dev vs build, agent mode vs server mode).
